video.title: He Makes $1M a Year Selling Fish From His Backyard

summary: UpFlip visits Ty at Smoking Chimneys (as transcribed), a revitalised 1930s federal trout hatchery on four acres in Newcastle, southwest Virginia, fed by a 3,000-gallon-a-minute limestone spring. With zero fish experience, Ty spent a year cleaning the site, a year learning to raise trout and a year getting state processing approval, burned through $60k of savings and worked at a grocery store before reaching $120k in sales; the farm now does $1.1M revenue with about $218k (19.8%) net margin, selling 85% fresh to Michelin-star and high-end restaurants and 15% frozen/smoked to co-ops, grocers and direct-to-consumer boxes. Growth came with no debt and no ads, using organic reels, chef referrals and in-person cooler drops. The key lesson was raising price from $11.50/lb (below a $15/lb cost) to $18/lb, which saved the business.

ideas.name: Spring-fed boutique trout farm selling to fine-dining restaurants
ideas.one_liner: Revive an old spring-fed trout hatchery and sell premium fresh and smoked trout to Michelin-star restaurants, grocers and consumers.
ideas.business_model: Product sales by the pound: wholesale to restaurants (85% fresh), frozen/smoked to co-ops, small grocers and direct-to-consumer boxes incl. a subscription
ideas.customer: High-end and Michelin-star restaurants across US cities; co-ops, small grocery stores, home consumers
ideas.problem: Farm-raised fish has a stigma; chefs want pristine, clean-tasting trout
ideas.offer: Whole fresh trout harvested weekly year-round, smoked fillets and whole smoked trout, brook trout on request

pricing.notes: Raised from $11.50 to $18 when cost was ~$15/lb; lost a few customers, mainly on the consumer/co-op side.

acquisition_channels.details: 2-3 reels a week showing how fish are raised, to overcome farm-fish stigma; no paid ads.

tactics.name: Know your cost per unit and price above it
steps: Run the numbers on full cost per pound (~$15)
Raise price from $11.50 to $18 so you earn a few dollars per pound
Accept losing a few customers; restaurants can absorb it better than retail co-ops

quote.text: if it's cost in 15, we need to make a couple bucks per pound to run our business
quote.speaker: Ty

tactics.name: Product-first pitch to chefs
steps: Show up in person with a cooler of fish
Explain briefly what you do
Let the chef taste it
Build exactly what top chefs ask for (raised brook trout over two years for Blue Hill)

quote.text: I would show up with the product, tell them a little bit about what we were doing, and then let them travel the trout
quote.speaker: Ty

tactics.name: Fixed weekly operating rhythm
steps: Monday: harvest, process, chill, pack, UPS
Tuesday: local deliveries and retail orders
Wednesday: smoking
Thursday/Friday: feed runs and pond work
Weekly one-hour weed trimming; check dissolved oxygen (target ~7.5-7.8 ppm)

tactics.name: Exit low-volume channels
steps: Calculate how much volume each channel can move
Quit farmers markets selling one or two fish at a time
Focus on bulk restaurant orders

quote.text: That was the single biggest contributor to me like quitting all farmers' markets
quote.speaker: Ty

tactics.name: Cheaper cold-chain packing
steps: Use ice packs instead of dry ice
Fill dead air space with paper
Replace any box that arrives warm

quote.text: Paper is really important, 'cause it's killing a lot of that dead air space
quote.speaker: Ty

tactics.name: Content to beat product stigma
steps: Post 2-3 reels a week showing natural raising conditions
Use content as the only marketing; no ads

warnings.warning: Underpricing below cost slowly bleeds a business out; he agonised six months before raising price.

quote.text: It probably took me six months of like agonizing to come to that decision
quote.speaker: Ty

warnings.warning: Inexperience killed fish early on; there were few resources for raising trout in an old system.

quote.text: We were killing more fish than what we were raising
quote.speaker: Ty

warnings.warning: Overgrown pond weeds cut oxygen and nearly suffocated a pond of fish.
It takes years before trout can be sold; cash burn on feed is heavy.

quote.text: This is years, you guys. Years before you could sell the trout
quote.speaker: Host

warnings.warning: Boutique farming has thin margins: you spend a lot to make a fraction.

lessons.lesson: Charging properly protects customers too, since they rely on you staying in business.

quote.text: you do your customers a disservice by not charging appropriately
quote.speaker: Ty

lessons.lesson: Take messy action and iterate; every wall is a turn in a maze.

quote.text: Take a messy action, whatever you do, it's not gonna be right, do it anyway. Then iterate
quote.speaker: Ty

lessons.lesson: Avoiding debt preserves creative freedom, at the cost of slower growth.

quote.text: I knew if I was in major debt, I wouldn't be able to like execute on the creative freedom
quote.speaker: Ty

lessons.lesson: A unique physical asset (the spring) is the moat; water quality drives taste.

quote.text: You have clean water, you're gonna have a clean product
quote.speaker: Ty

lessons.lesson: Pick channels that move volume; tiny retail sales can't cover fixed costs.
Deliver exactly what demanding flagship customers ask for to earn a reference account.
Things take much longer than expected; persistence through the low point matters.

quote.text: It's gonna take you way longer than what you thought it's gonna take, but you're going to get there
quote.speaker: Ty

lessons.lesson: Identify what you're really afraid of; fear keeps you in your current paradigm.
